topics.topic: Definition, provisioning, visibility, and path-rule treatment of own_proc
questions: What exactly is `own_proc`, how is it provided, and what must be visible or accessible through it?
What is `own_proc`: where and how is it mounted, what may function code read from it, and is it an exception to the audit hook's path rule?
Is agent code allowed to open paths in its own proc filesystem, and if so, which paths and with what mount/access restrictions?

precedent.topic: Definition, contents, and function-code accessibility of sandbox own_proc
quotes: execute_function: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST start bubblewrap with new user, PID, IPC, UTS and network namespaces and no network interface but the new namespace's own loopback, which bubblewrap brings up, with no capability option, the environment cleared and then set exactly to the imported SANDBOX_ENVIRONMENT constant, exactly the host paths of the imported SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS constant bound read-only, inside the new root the symbolic links of the imported SANDBOX_ROOT_SYMLINKS constant (each name linking to its target, made by bubblewrap --symlink), one fresh private exchange directory bound read-write, bubblewrap's own fresh proc mounted at the imported SANDBOX_PROC_MOUNT constant and minimal dev mounts, and no other host directory; the child dies with its parent, and the runner is the init of the new PID namespace (bubblewrap --as-pid-1), so bubblewrap exits only after the host kernel has killed and reaped every other process of that namespace.

The place is now `SANDBOX_PROC_MOUNT` in the data provider
    (`/proc`): `execute_function` mounts the proc there, `runner_arguments`
    passes it as the member `proc_directory`, and the runner lists it.
precedent.why: The later texts require bubblewrap's fresh private proc filesystem to be mounted at `/proc`.

topics.topic: Restart replay requirements for functions using time or chance
questions: Is equal output after restart guaranteed for every admitted function, or only for a function that obtains no time and no chance under a defined condition?
Must recovery reproduce the same output for functions that obtain time or chance through an untrapped mechanism, or may their recovered execution produce another conforming output?
May startup recovery of a function using an untrapped time or chance source produce a different conforming output, or must recovery guarantee or verify the same digest?

quotes:
The standard library's own entry points for the clock and for
randomness raise in a function, so it cannot depend on the time or on chance by
accident; code written to get time or chance some other way is not detected and is
judged by its outputs like any other.

Restarting the kernel during a function execution executes it again with the
   same output digest; during an effect it yields `unknown` and no second request.
judgement.divergence: Recovery accepts a different schema-valid output obtained through an untrapped source, or recovery must reproduce the interrupted execution's digest; the owner or agent reading the recovered run notices its output and downstream result.
judgement.why: The revised product rule permits undetected time- or chance-dependent code to be judged normally, while A14's unqualified recovery test requires the replayed execution to have the same digest.

witness.initial: An active run is executing an admitted function whose schema-valid output depends on an untrapped timing source, and no concluded NodeExecution has been recorded.
events: The function computes an output, but the kernel stops before recording its conclusion.
The kernel starts again and, as the kernel actor, re-executes the function element from the same pinned implementation and input.
The re-execution obtains a different timing value and returns a different schema-valid output.
outcomes: The different conforming output is judged like any other output and is accepted as the recovered run's output.
The recovered execution must have the same output digest as the interrupted execution.
witness.observer: The owner or agent reading the recovered run and its downstream result.
basis:
On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel turns every
   `in_flight` EffectAttempt into `unknown` (A11 rule 4) and then derives every
   run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `pending` — again
   from its records, oldest first in store order, rewriting a stored status or
   waiting point that lags them (a decided approval, a resolved attempt, an
   outcome whose run change was lost), and advances, as the
   kernel actor, every run that derivation leaves `running`: a
   function element without a
   concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it is pure; a `read`
   element without one is sent again; an operation element of another class with
   neither a concluded record nor an EffectAttempt was never sent and is advanced
   as if reached for the first time — an approved, unused approval covers it
   only while the rebuilt request has its `request_digest` (A10 rules 1 and 7).

judged by its outputs like any other.

topics.topic: Observable definition and detection of obtaining time or chance
questions: Which sources of varying output count as obtaining time or chance, and how can this condition be determined for an arbitrary implementation?
What observable criterion decides that an implementation "obtains no time and no chance", so the repeatability test can determine whether its same-digest requirement applies?

quotes:
An implementation that obtains no time and no chance yields the same output
   digest twice on the same input.

The standard library's own entry points for the clock and for
randomness raise in a function, so it cannot depend on the time or on chance by
accident; code written to get time or chance some other way is not detected and is
judged by its outputs like any other.
judgement.why: The texts lack an observable criterion for the test's precondition, but the proposed histories show the same trial outputs to the agent under either classification and do not establish two product behaviours observable by an owner, agent, caller or service.
